# The data pipeline example shows each stage and the worker that ran it

## Context

`examples/data/pipeline` is the only example that configures a `Neo.data.Pipeline`. It has no catalog record and was last changed in March 2026. #21140's target renews it for State & Data, with the operator's thought of 18 Nov: the pipeline made visible stage by stage. The band's epic #21358 counts it among its nine renewals. No leaf was filed.

## The Problem

The band's read ([its rows](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21142#issuecomment-6980292611)): "Two tabs, 'App Worker Pipeline' and 'Data Worker Pipeline', with the same four rows. Which worker parsed them cannot be seen." The data package can fetch, intercept, parse, normalize and cache off the app worker, and no page shows a visitor any of it. No example or app uses an interceptor.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/data/Pipeline.mjs` composes the stages; `src/data/interceptor/Base.mjs` is the interceptor base.
- `learn/guides/datahandling/DataPipelines.md` documents the pipeline and its interceptors: the example and the guide must agree.
- `examples/data/pipeline`: the folder to rebuild in place.

## The Fix

Rebuild the example in place with the pipeline as its subject. A payload large enough to matter, shipped with the example or generated in it. The page shows the run as a row of stages: the request, each interceptor hook that fired, the parser, the normalizer, the cache, each with what it did and how long it took, and the worker that ran it. A switch moves the parse between the app worker and the data worker, and a readout shows how long the app worker was busy in each case. The view at the pipeline's end stays plain, so the example repeats no grid example. It gets its record in State & Data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The page names every stage that ran, in order, with its duration and its worker.
- [ ] At least one interceptor is configured and its effect is visible on the page.
- [ ] The switch between the two workers changes the app worker's busy time on the page.
- [ ] The data ships with the example or is generated in it; no request leaves the host.
- [ ] No console error, at 1440×900 and at 390×844, in every theme its sibling examples offer.
- [ ] A record in State & Data with a caption in the visitor's words and a cover from its first frame (through `neomjs/pages`).
- [ ] The look: the first frame and the frame after a run on each worker, Neo Dark, on the pull request, read cold by the reviewer's seat.

**Publication (added 22 Nov, the same for every leaf of this wave).** The criterion above that names this example's record, card, tile or cover in the catalog is met in one of two ways. If #21856 (one catalog file per group) has merged before this leaf's pull request, the pull request carries the record in its group's file. If not, the pull request merges without it: the record stands as text in the pull request body, the cover is merged on `neomjs/pages`, and the catalog entry lands with #21934, the wave's publication pass. Either way this leaf closes with its example.

## Out of Scope

A change to the pipeline's API, except the seven additive fields of the opt-in `telemetry` sample named in the intake's Contract Ledger (comment 7079826733). The guide ladder for the data package (#21140, "After the cut", item 3). A grid at the pipeline's end.

## Avoided Traps

- **A big grid as the result.** Grid & Table already shows a simulated server and a streamed load; this example's subject is what happens before the rows arrive.

Prescription checked: `src/data/Pipeline.mjs` — owns the concern (`profile()`, `measureStage()`, `publishTelemetry()`).

**Read for this intake:** `src/data/Pipeline.mjs` whole; `Store.mjs` (pipeline config, load, `readResponse`), `Model.mjs` (config), `interceptor/Base.mjs`, `connection/Base.mjs`, `connection/Fetch.mjs`, `parser/Base.mjs`, `normalizer/Base.mjs`, `worker/Data.mjs` (module loading), `list/Base.mjs` (item content); the guide's worker and interceptor sections; siblings `examples/grid/serverSide`, `examples/grid/streaming`, `examples/worker/canvas`. Not read whole in this session: `core/Base.mjs`, `Neo.mjs`, `state/Provider.mjs`; the example uses reactive configs with their `afterSet` hooks and no provider.

### Investigation 3 of #21140: what a pipeline reports per stage

1. **It reports three stages.** With `telemetry: true` the App-side pipeline fires one `telemetry` sample per attempt, on either worker: start and end of `connection`, `parser` and `normalizer`, `rawSize` and `parsedSize` (bytes for strings and binary values, record counts for arrays), `operation`, `status`.
2. **It does not say where it ran, and it does not time the hooks.** No field names the executing realm. The interceptor hooks run outside the three measured stages, so with interceptors the stage times no longer add up to the attempt. A cache hit is not marked either.
3. **An interceptor's effect shows without engine work, its time does not.** `rawSize` is taken after the response hooks and `parsedSize` after `postParse`, so "500,000 orders became 8 rows" can be read from a sample. How long the hook took cannot.
4. **An app's own class reaches a Data-worker pipeline only as an interceptor.** `createRemoteExecution` preloads connection, parser and normalizer through `loadDataModule`, which admits `Neo.data.*` classes only; interceptors alone take a `modulePath`. So the example's own shaping lives in an interceptor. A finding for its own ticket, not for this leaf.
5. **Parsing alone does not stall an app.** Measured in headless Chromium: 48 MB of JSON parse in about 50 to 80 ms, and a report over 500,000 orders (a date parsed per order, grouped per country) takes about 100 ms. So the payload "large enough to matter" needs real shaping work; a bigger file would only cost memory. Two platform facts decide the data source: a `blob:` URL fails to fetch once it carries a query string, and one worker can fetch a blob URL another worker created.

### Scope

The card is the example plus a small engine addition, because the page has to name every stage "with its duration and its worker" and the hook that shapes the data is where the time goes. Two buttons instead of one switch: a run per worker, and both results stay on the page. The "app worker busy" readout is a heartbeat the app beats itself in the App Worker. No cache stage: the example configures none, so no marker is added for it.

### Contract Ledger: the `telemetry` sample of `Neo.data.Pipeline`

| Field | Before | After | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `worker` | absent | `Neo.workerId` of the realm that ran the attempt; `null` outside a worker | `Pipeline#profile` |
| `requestStart`, `requestEnd` | absent | the request hook chain; `null` without handlers and for a push | `Pipeline#runLocal` |
| `responseStart`, `responseEnd` | absent | the response or responseError chain; `null` without handlers or without a connection call | `Pipeline#runStages` |
| `postParseStart`, `postParseEnd` | absent | the post-parse chain; `null` without handlers, and for a stream, whose chunks are transformed inside the parser stage | `Pipeline#runStages` |

Additive and opt-in (`telemetry: true`); existing fields keep their meaning. Surface-anchor check: `fire('telemetry'` and `pipelineTelemetry` have no consumer in `src/`, `apps/` or `examples/` besides the Logger passthrough; the pinned key list in `PipelineTelemetry.spec.mjs` is extended, and a new test reads the hook times in flow order.

**Scope reconciliation asked by the review of PR #21950 (its RA-3): a proposed restatement of "Out of Scope", for the ticket's author to apply or confirm.**

The body excludes "A change to the pipeline's API". The pull request adds seven fields to the opt-in `telemetry` sample of `Neo.data.Pipeline`: `worker`, and the start and end of the `request`, `response` and `postParse` hook chains (`requestStart`, `requestEnd`, `responseStart`, `responseEnd`, `postParseStart`, `postParseEnd`). They are additive, exist only with `telemetry: true`, and change no existing field and no carrier. Their ledger is in the [intake comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21880#issuecomment-7079826733).

Why the example needs them: the sample timed connection, parser and normalizer. The example's work, shaping the orders into a report, runs in the post-parse hook, so the page would have shown no time for the stage where the time goes, and it could not have named the worker from the sample itself.
